prompt:
Below is a policy summary from a UK general election manifesto. Identify the party that produced it. You must choose one.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core mission
- Get Brexit done: Pass the “oven‑ready” deal, leave the EU in January 2020, no extension beyond Dec 2020. Outside the single market, customs union and ECJ; UK makes its own laws, controls money, borders and trade. Seek a zero-tariff FTA with the EU and parallel deals with the US, Australia, New Zealand and Japan. Oppose second referendums on Brexit and Scottish independence. Strengthen the Union.

Economy and tax
- Invest but keep debt under control; no borrowing for day-to-day spending; public investment capped at 3% of GDP.
- No rises in the main rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise NI threshold to £9,500 next year; ambition that the first £12,500 you earn is tax-free.
- Support small firms: fundamental review to cut business rates; stronger late-payment enforcement; expand start-up loans; increase Employment Allowance; maintain SEIS/EIS; raise R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneur’s Relief; Digital Services Tax; tougher anti‑avoidance laws.

Public services
- NHS: Record funding (+£34bn by 2023/24); 50,000 more nurses, 6,000 more GPs and 6,000 more primary care professionals; 50m extra GP appointments; 40 new hospitals/20 upgrades; NHS Visa; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health parity; prevention and screening; free hospital parking for priority groups; clamp down on health tourism; NHS not on the table in trade talks.
- Social care: Extra £1bn per year; cross-party reform with guarantee no one has to sell their home; one week’s leave for unpaid carers; double dementia research.
- Schools: +£14bn over three years; per‑pupil minimums; teacher starting salary to £30k; behaviour/Ofsted backing; arts premium; PE investment; more SEND support; more free schools and alternative provision.

Crime and justice
- 20,000 more police; more stop-and-search (fair, proportionate); new knife crime orders; tougher sentencing (end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; whole‑life terms for child murder); 10,000 extra prison places; parole reform; National Cyber Force; Victims’ Law; online harms regulation; tackle county lines and organised crime; powers on unauthorised encampments.

Immigration
- Australian-style points-based system; reduce low‑skilled migration; equal EU/non‑EU treatment; 5‑year wait for most benefits; higher NHS surcharge; fast‑track visas for NHS staff and top global talent; Windrush compensation; student and start‑up visas.

Infrastructure, housing and places
- “Infrastructure revolution”: Northern Powerhouse Rail (Leeds–Manchester first), Midlands Rail Hub, roads, EV rapid‑charging network, bus upgrades, cycling fund, gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025; review HS2; reverse some Beeching cuts; contactless ticketing.
- Towns/High Streets: Towns Fund; Safer Streets Fund; youth services; cultural investment; Community Ownership Fund; devolution White Paper; City/Growth Deals; up to 10 freeports.
- Housing: Target 300,000 homes/year; long‑term fixed‑rate mortgages for first‑time buyers; First Homes 30% local discount; renters’ reform (end “no‑fault” evictions; lifetime deposit); social housing white paper; end rough sleeping by end of Parliament; building safety post‑Grenfell; green, tree‑lined streets; protect Green Belt; stamp duty surcharge for non‑resident buyers.

Skills, work and innovation
- £3bn National Skills Fund; upgrade FE estate (£2bn); 20 Institutes of Technology; apprentices on major projects; Shared Prosperity Fund.
- Fair work: right to request predictable contracts; single enforcement body; more flexible working; neonatal leave; extend unpaid carers’ leave; protect from maternity discrimination.
- Science/innovation: fastest-ever rise in R&D to reach 2.4% of GDP; new high‑risk research agency; life sciences hub; unleash pension capital; Festival UK 2022; use procurement to back innovation.

Rural, farming, fishing and environment
- Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; protect farm budgets; expand seasonal workers scheme; leave CFP; sustainable fishing; rural broadband/mobile; tackle rural crime.
- Climate and nature: Net Zero by 2050; Environment Bill and new watchdog; £640m Nature for Climate; 75,000 acres of trees/year; plastics crackdown, deposit return, ban plastic waste exports to non‑OECD; £9.2bn for home/school/hospital efficiency; offshore wind 40GW by 2030; first CCS cluster by mid‑2020s; support hydrogen and nuclear; EV infrastructure; stricter air quality laws; fracking moratorium; £4bn flood defences; £500m Blue Planet Fund.

Constitution, defence and foreign policy
- Restore trust: repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; voter ID; equalised constituencies; keep First Past the Post; strengthen free press (repeal s.40; no Leveson 2); constitutional review incl. courts/HR Act/judicial review.
- Defence: exceed NATO 2% with real increases; modernise forces; Trident; Space Command; cyber; support veterans (legal protections, NI relief for employers, childcare, railcard, guaranteed interviews).
- Global role: champion free trade and human rights; 0.7% aid; Magnitsky sanctions; girls’ education; modern slavery/media freedom; support persecuted faith/LGBT conference; back major sporting bids.

Animal welfare
- Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end long live‑animal exports; extend ivory ban; ban primates as pets; measures on cat microchipping/theft.
</text>

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else, with these keys in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<what in the text informed your choice>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "party": one of ['Conservative', 'Labour', 'Liberal Democrats', 'Scottish National Party', 'Green Party']
}
